newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - GUS sees merger enhancing earnings.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - GUS sees merger enhancing earnings.

text.p: British retailer Great Universal Stores Plc (GUS) said on Thursday that the $1.7 billion merger of its information services business, CCN, with U.S. company Experian would be earnings-enhancing in the first year.
GUS's payment for the credit, marketing and real estate information services will be financed through an $800 million loan with the rest coming from its own existing resources.

"If GUS had not bought Experian, then Experian would have liked to have bought CCN, because the natural fit of the two companies is quite outstanding," Lord Wolfson, chairman of GUS, told Reuters in a telephone interview.

Wolfson said that CCN and Experian had been talking to each other for several years. "It really matured into serious conversations in the summer of this year and it has taken a few months to reach full agreement."
He estimated that the combined business would make up around 15 to 20 percent of the entire GUS group. "In other words it is a major core division."

GUS, whose businesses include Burberry's and Scotch House as well as four mail order catalogue units, set up CCN in 1980 to satisfy demand from banks, retailers and other lenders for credit information on their customers.
